Well, I'm 55 this year, and I've been farming these ten mu and a bit since I was fifteen helping my old man. It's just me and my wife at home now — our son works at a factory in Handan, sends a bit back when he can, but not much. The land is flat with good soil, but fertilizer prices keep going up and electricity for the pump isn't cheap either. Every yuan I spend is a yuan I can't use if someone gets sick, so I think carefully.

For the wheat, I always plant right after National Day, around October 12th. The soil is still warm then and the wheat gets established before winter. I buy improved seed from the shop in town — usually Jimai or whatever variety they have that isn't too expensive, about 30 yuan per mu. I don't experiment with new seeds; what I know works. For fertilizer, I put down base fertilizer before sowing: about 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu, the 15-15-15 kind. Then at jointing time around Qingming, I topdress with urea, about 25 kg per mu. The extension fellow told me last year that 20 kg of urea is enough, but I've been doing 25 kg for years and last year I got around 430 kg per mu — why would I change now? That's maybe around 17 kg of nitrogen per mu total? I don't calculate it exactly, I just know the bags. I also get phosphorus and potassium from the compound fertilizer.

I'll irrigate the wheat three times: once right after sowing to get good germination, once at jointing when the weather warms up, and once at grain filling if it doesn't rain. Each irrigation costs me electricity money, maybe 20 yuan per mu, so that's over 600 yuan just for wheat irrigation. But dry wheat means low yield, and I'd rather waste some money on water than lose half the crop.

For maize, the problem is always the rush after wheat harvest. I hire a combine to cut the wheat — costs about 40 yuan per mu, but it's fast. Then I need to get the maize in within two or three days, otherwise the growing season gets too short. I do quick rotary tillage, then plant immediately. I buy hybrid seed, about 45 yuan per mu. For fertilizer, I put it all down at planting — compound fertilizer and urea together. This year fertilizer is expensive, so I'm cutting back a bit on the maize to save cash for the wheat: about 40 kg of compound and 20 kg of urea per mu. That's a bit less than last year, but maize is tougher than wheat. If the leaves look yellow at the big flare stage, maybe I'll add a little more, but usually I don't have time. I'll irrigate maize twice — once in July if it's dry, and once at silking. If the rains are good, maybe once is enough.

For pesticides, I spray herbicide on both crops. For wheat, I do it in early spring. For maize, right after emergence. If I see corn borer, I'll spray insecticide. I keep an eye out for rust but I didn't need fungicide last year.

Labor is mostly me and my wife. But during wheat harvest and maize planting, the rush is too much for just us, so I hire two workers for a couple of days — now it's 150 yuan per day plus meals. During maize harvest in late September, the combine does most of the work, but we still need to haul the grain home.

Total costs this year... seed about 750 yuan, fertilizer about 3,000 yuan, pesticide about 500 yuan, irrigation about 1,000 yuan, hired labor and machinery about 1,500 yuan. That's roughly 6,800 yuan. It's a lot, but I have some savings from last year. I expect wheat to give me about 430 kg per mu and maize about 480 kg per mu, similar to last year if the weather holds.
